approach: Root cause, written in the same words in new decision D189 and in the CHANGELOG entry: criteria are checked independently only after the producer ends, so an unmet criterion found by the verifier cannot trigger a repair. `produce_and_verify` (run/mod.rs:1871-1950) runs one producer loop, one candidate, one set of checks and one verifier, and `close_dispatched` (run/close.rs:46-55) closes a fail verdict as Rejected. Only the producer's own report is ever sent back (`unmet_criteria`, run/send_back.rs:19, used at producer.rs:465). The 43 introspections ask for a pre-verdict self-check, but the producer's self-report is already checked; what is missing is the independent verdict reaching the producer while a round is left to use it. Fix, in the run pipeline, bounded, with no refusal rule. (a) `produce_and_verify` keeps baseline and disk gate once and moves one round (snapshot, producer loop, candidate, remove work tree, `Built`, resume mark, `check_and_verify`) into `produce_round(.., seed, repair)`. (b) After round one a pure `verify::repair_view(&Verification) -> Option<RepairView>` reads the stored verdict. It is Some only when the verifier judged (`agent_verdict` Some), the final verdict is Fail and a repairable item is left: an unmet criterion or a blocker or major finding, after dropping three kinds the producer cannot change (unassessed criterion, D43 'cited but not seen running' criterion, request misread). (c) While fewer than the new `VERIFIER_REPAIRS` (=1, beside `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, mod.rs:1681) repairs have run, and not nested, and `preflight(Run)` and the disk gate pass, it saves round one's candidate, verification and happened state, writes the first-round items into the first verifier invocation's `detail`, removes the job's resume mark, and runs round two from a snapshot seeded with the first candidate (`SnapshotRepo::BaseThenTree`, producer.rs:144-153). Round two's brief comes from `send_back_text_repaired`, the new last link of the existing send-back chain, and the same view is passed into `producer_loop`, so round two's own send-back keeps one `## Sent back` heading. (d) If round two reaches a verdict, that verdict is final and a fail names all first-round items in the closing reason. If round two ends before a verdict (producer stop, admission, gate or scope stop), round one's candidate and Verification are restored and the job stays Rejected, with round two's stop reason and the repair note in the reason, so a retry still has the first candidate and the verifier's findings.

decisions.choice: Repair loop wraps one round in `produce_and_verify`; the trigger is the pure `verify::repair_view` over the stored `Verification`, not a new field carried out of `verification_stage`.
decisions.reason: Everything the trigger needs is already in the record: `agent_verdict` is Some exactly when the verifier returned output (verify.rs:639), a timeout or incomplete verifier leaves it None, `request_reading_mismatch` is Some only for a real misread (verification.rs:442-448). Reusing the whole round keeps admission, the decision gate, the checks, the replay and the pull-request replace identical for the second candidate. A `closing.verification` that is Some after round two always means a verdict was reached, because round one's is taken out before round two and every early stop in `check_and_verify` (mod.rs:1992-2056) and `candidate_stage` (candidate.rs:179, 222) leaves it None. Existing code already treats a misread and an unmet or unseen Behavior criterion as not retryable from the tree (`qualifies_for_tree_retry`, retry.rs:347-359), so the exclusions match what the repo already means by 'a producer pass cannot fix it'.

rejected.option: Set a typed `Closing.repair` inside `verification_stage`

rejected.option: Re-run only the verifier with a producer pass inside `verification_stage`
rejected.why: It has no producer snapshot, grant or prompt and would skip candidate, admission and checks for the repaired tree.

rejected.option: Raise PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS and send back on the producer's own report
rejected.why: That is the self-report direction the dropped jobs took; the failing signal is the independent verdict, which exists only after verification.

decisions.choice: New `const VERIFIER_REPAIRS: u32 = 1` beside `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, enforced by a counter. No repair for a nested run, a resumed candidate, a failed `preflight(Run)` or low disk (one `repair     skipped: ...` line for the last two). Before round two starts the job's resume mark is removed (`self.state.remove_resume(&id)`, state.rs:315).
decisions.reason: The bound is in code and named (criterion 5, mechanism default). `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS` is documented (mod.rs:1677-1681) as the shared pre-verifier send-back and D182 keeps it at 1, so it is not reused. `preflight(Run)` (reading.rs:502-515; reserve = producer + verifier caps) means no repair starts that the job budget cannot pay; the live `athena.toml` has producer 10.00, verifier 5.00, job 50.00 (lines 45-47), so a normal job can pay. A nested run is judged by the outer job, the same guard as mod.rs:1980, 2006, 2028. `resume_candidate` (mod.rs:843-844) calls `check_and_verify` directly and never reaches the loop. Finding 4: round one writes a resume mark for the first candidate (mod.rs:1948) and `settle_resume_marks` keeps a mark only for a Failed environment stop (mod.rs:886). Without removal, a round-two hold or environment stop would let `athena retry` resume the already-rejected first candidate and spend a verifier on it with no repair. Removing the mark first means: a hold before round two's candidate is admitted leaves no mark and the next drain starts from the start (the documented pre-producer hold, close.rs:170-176); once round two's candidate is admitted `produce_round` writes a mark that points at round two's candidate; a Failed stop in round two is restored to Rejected (decision 3) so `settle_resume_marks` removes the mark. D189 states this.

rejected.option: Reuse PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 2
rejected.why: It would give the producer's own report two send-backs and change every send-back test and D182.

rejected.option: Unbounded repair until the verifier passes
rejected.why: Unbounded cost; the reading says one round.

rejected.option: Hold the job for low disk before round two
rejected.why: A hold before a producer means no candidate yet (close.rs:170-176), so the first verdict would be thrown away; skipping keeps the first verdict.

rejected.option: Leave round one's resume mark in place
rejected.why: A retry would resume the first, already rejected candidate with no repair (finding 4).

decisions.choice: Store the repair as ordinary records, with no new record type or field, and keep round one's candidate and Verification until round two produces a new Verification. (1) The first verifier's `Invocation.detail` lists every unmet criterion and blocking finding (no count cap, each item clipped to 240 chars) and says the work was sent back for one repair pass. (2) `Closing::put_file` replaces same-path files, so round two's verifier brief and replay record replace round one's. (3) Before round two a `FirstRound { candidate, verification, happened }` clone is taken and `closing.candidate`, `closing.verification` and `closing.verified` are cleared. (4) If round two returns with a Verification, the job closes on it; a fail has reason `the final verdict is fail: {second reasons}. {note}`. (5) If round two returns with no Verification, the clone is restored: round one's candidate and Verification, state Rejected, `verification_passed` Some(false), reason `the final verdict is fail: {first reasons}. {note}; the repair pass stopped before a verdict: {round two's stop reason}`. (6) If round two returns an error (a hold), `commit_hold` takes the closing as it is, with no Verification and no candidate, as a hold before a producer does.
decisions.reason: Finding 3: `candidate_stage` sets `closing.candidate` to round two's candidate on every path (candidate.rs:178, 220, 227) and each stop replaces `closing.happened` through `self.failure` (state Failed, mod.rs:2581-2591), so without the restore a repaired job whose second producer fails would close Failed with no Verification, and `tree_retry_seed` returns None without one (retry.rs:410-412). With the restore the job ends where it ended today: Rejected with the first candidate and verifier findings, so `qualifies_for_tree_retry` (retry.rs:330-370) and `tree_retry_seed` (retry.rs:392-443) see round one; `attempt_of` (scope_guard.rs) and `failure_details` (introspect.rs:1048-1117) read the same record. Restoring to Rejected also covers a round-two timeout: the first verdict stands, the retry seeds from round one's candidate. `Happened`, `Candidate` and `Verification` are Clone (scoring.rs:133, records.rs:848, 933). `Invocation.detail` is the existing redacted free text of how an invocation ended (invocation.rs:152-157); the producer already stores a self-check failure on a successful invocation (producer.rs:614-625). The introspector builds `what` from `outcome.reason` plus `failure_details(verification)` and never reads `detail` (introspect.rs:1538-1572), so the reason carries all first-round items (finding 7: no count cap, only each item's length is clipped). The prefix `the final verdict is fail:` stays first (close.rs:53). The note is redacted with the job's redactor before it is stored. Round one's Verification is replaced by round two's because its path is per job (records.rs:934); the note names the first candidate's short commit, the first verifier, the repair producer's first seq and the final verifier.

rejected.option: Take round one's Verification out and leave it out when round two stops (the previous plan)
rejected.why: The job would close Failed with no Verification and a retry would lose the first candidate and the verifier's blocking findings.

rejected.option: Keep both Verification records
rejected.why: The path is per job; a second would overwrite it or need a new path and an allow-list change in athena-data.

rejected.option: Add a typed `repair` field to Invocation or Verification
rejected.why: It changes athena-data record shapes and every stored-record reader for information the detail and reason text already carry.

rejected.option: Push the repair note into `Verification.reasons`
rejected.why: It would put a reason on a passing verification and change what the landing gate and `verified()` see.

rejected.option: Cap the note at 3 items
rejected.why: A first round with four or more items would again leave an unmet criterion out of the stored event, the failure class being fixed (finding 7).

decisions.choice: The repair brief extends the existing builder chain: `send_back_text_scoped` becomes a wrapper over a new last link `send_back_text_repaired(.., repair: Option<&RepairView>)`, and the same `Option<&RepairView>` is passed into `producer_loop`, which uses it for its first attempt brief and for its own send-backs (the four-arm match at producer.rs:684-700 becomes one call, which the four wrappers' None-equivalence pins). With None the text is byte-identical. With Some, one `## Sent back` heading holds the repair intro (it replaces the 'Your previous report...' paragraph) then the lists.
decisions.reason: The shared intro is false for a repair: 'your previous report did not show every criterion met', 'This is the only send-back' and 'A run that leaves no change fails' (send_back.rs:162-173); a seeded run that adds nothing is the candidate, not an idle producer (candidate.rs:168-181). The base snapshot text says 'a snapshot of the base commit's files' (briefs.rs:710-714) while the seeded one is the base plus the candidate's files laid over it, uncommitted (snapshot.rs:97-101). The intro states four facts: the directory is a fresh snapshot already holding the first candidate (`git diff` against its base shows it); the independent verifier, not the producer's report, found the items; a run that adds nothing keeps the first candidate and it is verified again unchanged; the verdict after this round is final. Finding 8: `producer_loop` builds its own send-back from the `brief` it is given (producer.rs:684-700), so if round two's brief were already a repair text the result would hold two `## Sent back` headings and the old 'only send-back' sentences. Passing the view in keeps one heading; items from the producer's own report in this round are listed under the existing 'Criteria not met or not reported' and 'Planned files left unchanged' headings, after the repair intro, and `append_mirror_drift` (send_back.rs:227-247) still finds one heading. The findings block is shared with `must_address_block` (briefs.rs:616-629) and each finding is formatted by `finding_text` (retry.rs:446), so a finding reads the same in a retry and in a repair; the texts pass through `ctx.redactor` as `tree_retry_seed` does (retry.rs:424).

rejected.option: A separate `repair_brief` function
rejected.why: A parallel builder, contrary to criterion 5.

rejected.option: Only prepend one sentence to the shared intro
rejected.why: The rest of that intro would stay false.

rejected.option: Build round two's brief as a repair text and let `producer_loop` nest its own send-back under it
rejected.why: Two `## Sent back` headings and contradicting sentences (finding 8).

rejected.option: A new formatter for findings in briefs.rs
rejected.why: It would describe the same finding differently from the retry brief.

decisions.choice: Trigger: a judged Fail verdict with an unmet criterion or a blocker or major finding, after dropping what a producer pass cannot change: (i) a criterion the verifier did not assess and its Athena 'Criterion N was not assessed' finding; (ii) a criterion that got the Athena D43 finding ('Behavior criterion N is unmet: its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43)') and that finding; (iii) the Athena request-misread finding. A failing check repairs only through the verifier: when the verifier marks a criterion unmet (for example 'fmt, clippy and test pass') or adds a blocker or major finding, the repair runs; a failing check that the verifier did not flag as an unmet criterion or a serious finding triggers none. Athena's own blockers and majors that a producer can fix (held replay, a requirement row marked Covered) stay in.
decisions.reason: `judge` fails the verdict on exactly these items (verify.rs:649-664). Finding 5: `judge` adds only a Minor finding for a failing check (verify.rs:448-473) and the check fails the verdict through `reasons`, so my earlier claim that a failing check alone never repairs was true only when the verifier ignored it; most readings carry a check criterion the verifier marks unmet, so the repair does run then, and the producer already had the check output once in the loop (`loop_check_failures`). D189 and the CHANGELOG say this. Finding 6: the D43 flip sets `met = false` where the verifier's cited commands were not seen running or it cited none (verify.rs:585-605); that describes what the verifier ran, as 'not assessed' does (verify.rs:549-555), and nothing a producer pass changes decides it, so it is excluded from the trigger and from the lists. The stored record cannot tell a criterion the verifier itself judged unmet and that also cites no command from one Athena flipped, so such a criterion is repaired only when the verifier also gives a blocker or major finding or another listed item. That is the one known gap; D189 and the CHANGELOG name it and it is not measured. The three Athena summaries become shared consts or fns used by both `judge` and `repair_view` so they cannot drift.

rejected.option: Trigger on every blocker or major finding
rejected.why: Repairs a misread, an unassessed criterion or a D43 flip at full cost with no way to change the outcome.

rejected.option: Trigger on a failed check as well
rejected.why: The producer already had one send-back with the check's output tail before the verifier; the verifier's unmet check criterion already triggers a repair.

rejected.option: Keep D43 items as triggers (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Same kind of verifier omission as 'not assessed' and a brief that tells the producer to fix something it cannot change (finding 6).

rejected.option: Exclude check criteria (`is_athena_check_criterion`) from the trigger
rejected.why: A failing fmt, clippy or test check is a producer-fixable cause and the most common unmet criterion in the 43 introspections.
